articles.title: India's First Large-Scale Biopolymer Plant Set for October Launch - GKToday
articles.content: Home India’s First Large-Scale Biopolymer Plant Set for October Launch India’s First Large-Scale Biopolymer Plant Set for October Launch August 21, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 India’s first large-scale biopolymer plant is under construction in Lakhimpur Kheri district of Uttar Pradesh and is scheduled for commissioning in October 2026. The facility is being developed at the Kumbhi sugar unit of Balrampur Chini Mills in Gola Gokarannath and is planned as a fully integrated industrial campus. Biopolymer and PLA Biopolymers are polymers derived from renewable biological sources such as plant biomass, starch, or sugar-based feedstock. The plant will convert locally grown sugarcane into sugar and then into Polylactic Acid, commonly called PLA, which is a biodegradable thermoplastic used in packaging and disposable products. Project Location and Development The foundation stone for the project was laid on 22 February 2025 by Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The site is located within the Kumbhi sugar unit, which links sugar production with downstream bioplastic manufacturing on the same campus. The project cost has been cited at ₹3,080 crore in recent official references, while early 2025 estimates placed it at ₹2,850 crore. Lakhimpur Kheri District Magistrate Anjani Kumar Singh inspected the facility on 20 August 2026 to review production workflows, technical layouts, and construction progress. Industrial Features and Output The plant will use a Zero Liquid Discharge system, or ZLD, which is an industrial wastewater management method in which liquid effluent is not released outside the facility. The project is designed to manufacture products such as plates, cups, and bags that decompose naturally within three to six months. Commercial output of biodegradable products is expected to begin in November 2026 after the October commissioning. The facility is part of India’s industrial shift towards bio-based materials derived from agricultural feedstock. Important Facts for Exams Polylactic Acid is a biodegradable polyester made from renewable resources such as corn starch or sugarcane. Zero Liquid Discharge is used in industries to minimise wastewater release into the environment. Balrampur Chini Mills is one of India’s major sugar companies with operations linked to sugarcane processing. Bioplastic products are used in packaging, disposable tableware, and carry bags. Industrial and Environmental Context Sugarcane is a major commercial crop in Uttar Pradesh and is used in sugar, ethanol, and bio-based industrial products. PLA-based bioplastics are classified as bio-based materials because they originate from renewable agricultural feedstock rather than fossil fuels. articles.title: DPA Kandla hosts 2026 Green Hydrogen Conclave - The News Mill
articles.content: ANI Photo | DPA Kandla hosts Kandla Green Hydrogen Conclave 2026 to advance maritime decarbonisation Deendayal Port Authority (DPA), Kandla, organised the Kandla Green Hydrogen Conclave 2026 on Friday at its Administrative Office Building in Gandhidham, Gujarat. The event brought together global thought leaders, industry experts and delegates to discuss clean energy and sustainable maritime development. The conclave began with a virtual address from Union Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal and was attended by Sushil Kumar Singh, Chairman of DPA Kandla; Erik Solheim, former Minister of the Kingdom of Norway and President of the International Advisory Board for GH2 India; along with other dignitaries. ADVERTISEMENT Stay connected Make The News Mill your preferred source See more TNM stories when you search for news on Google. Add TNM on Google Participants engaged in detailed discussions on green hydrogen, clean energy transition, sustainable port development and emerging green technologies. The event aimed to foster international collaboration and share ideas to accelerate India’s green maritime ambitions, according to DPA Kandla. As part of the conclave, the GH2 delegation visited India’s first Make-in-India 1-MW Green Hydrogen Plant at Kandla and toured key port facilities to assess DPA’s infrastructure, operations and increasing focus on green energy and sustainability. ADVERTISEMENT Chairman Sushil Kumar Singh emphasised the need to adopt greener fuels and energy-efficient technologies to reduce the maritime sector’s carbon footprint. He stated, “As we all know, the maritime sector contributes around three per cent of the total green hydrogen gas annually, and it’s one of the sectors which has to take initiative to bring down the Greenhouse gas (GHG) intensity in line with the Paris Agreement where the member countries and member states have agreed to restrict the temperature rise to ambient increase below 1.5 degrees Celsius.” Singh highlighted the limitations of energy efficiency technologies, noting that they “cannot translate into a zero-emission kind of output.” He added, “The adoption of greener fuels, cleaner fuels, sustainable zero-emission fuels, along with the energy-efficient technologies that can help in bringing down the carbon footprint of operations in the maritime sector, that becomes important. The energy efficiency component of the technologies has its own limitations; it cannot translate into a zero-emission kind of output. So, the adoption of greener fuels is essential.” Written by TNM (With ANI Inputs) This story is written by TNM Bureau with inputs from ANI. articles.title: Fairmont Mumbai and Le Florence India Hosted India's First Longevity Summit 2026 with AIWO
articles.content: VMPL Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], August 21: The inaugural Longevity Summit India 2026 unfolded over two immersive days at Fairmont Mumbai, bringing together 1,000+ delegates from India and across the global longevity ecosystem for a convergence of science, healthcare, wellness, technology and conscious living. Presented by Le Florence India in partnership with Fairmont Mumbai, with AIWO as the Title Sponsor, Maharashtra Tourism as the State Partner, and DecodeAge as the Wellness Partner, the summit brought together international experts, leading doctors, scientists, biohackers, wellness practitioners, founders, investors and thought leaders through global panels, expert talks, fireside conversations, experiential zones, longevity trails and interactive practices. Far beyond a conventional conference, the experience transformed Fairmont Mumbai into an immersive landscape of longevity, from underwater meditation, Watsu, ice plunges, yoga and sound experiences to explorations of biological age, metabolic health, brain performance, emotional resilience, and human connection. Even the culinary experience was designed around wellbeing, with colour-coded Yellow, Green and White food zones, each focused on supporting different functions of the body, from digestion and metabolic health to heart health. At its core, the summit explored a question increasingly shaping the future of healthcare: how do we not simply live longer, but extend healthspan, preserve vitality and improve the quality of the years we live? The programme brought together preventive healthcare, geroscience, human optimisation, performance engineering of the body, bio-optimisation and functional enhancement, examining the interconnected systems that influence how we age, perform and experience life. The summit's philosophy was reflected in its Five Bodies Framework: Earth, Water, Air, Fire and Flow, offering a more holistic, systems-based lens on longevity. Rather than viewing health through isolated biomarkers or individual interventions, the framework examined how multiple physiological and psychological systems interact to influence resilience, vitality, and long-term healthspan. The conversation around longevity also extended into how people live and age, with senior living emerging as an important part of the wider ecosystem. The summit saw the launch of Shremoha, a premium senior independent living platform formed in July 2026 through a strategic partnership between Shrem Group and Emoha, part of Age Care Labs. Unveiled through the thought leadership panel "The New Luxury of Longevity: How Senior Living is Becoming the World's Most Powerful Platform for Healthy Ageing," Shremoha brings together geriatric-grade personalised care, preventive health, wellness, and hospitality-led living to support greater independence, purpose and dignity among India's seniors. Nitan Chhatwal, MD, Shrem Group and Co-founder of Shremoha, said, " Senior living is no longer the destination after ageing; it is a platform for longevity. With Shremoha, we are bringing hospitality, wellness and geriatric care together to create communities built around independence, purpose and possibility." Saumyajit Roy, Co-founder & CEO, Emoha Elder Care and Co-founder of Shremoha, said, "The future of senior living is not about care alone, but about creating places where people can live with purpose, independence and meaningful connections. Shremoha brings our experience in elder care together with hospitality and community design to build exactly that." The idea of longevity extending beyond healthcare...

articles.title: Sprite Tejas Express: India's first branded train flagged off on Lucknow–New Delhi route
articles.content: New Delhi: Train journeys in India are getting a new branding twist. The Sprite Tejas Express, billed as India’s first branded train, was flagged off on Thursday, bringing together the soft drink brand’s identity with one of Indian Railways’ premium train services. Getting onboard the Sprite Tejas Express The train will operate on the Lucknow–New Delhi–Lucknow route for six months from August, with five coaches carrying Sprite branding on their exteriors. The train will also be announced as the Sprite Tejas Express at originating and en route stations on both legs of its journey. What’s in it for passengers? The partnership between Sprite and the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) goes beyond putting a logo on a moving train. Sprite will be part of the passenger food bundle, while the launch included complimentary Sprite samples and merchandise for travellers. The brand said further Sprite-led experiences will also be introduced onboard. The association gives the beverage brand a presence across a busy travel corridor used by business travellers, tourists and families, while offering IRCTC a new form of brand partnership within the passenger experience. From station benches to a flag made from bottles The branding also comes with a sustainability element. As part of the initiative, benches at the station have been made using recycled plastic, with each bench repurposing about 45 kg of post-consumer packaging waste. Even the ceremonial flag used during the train’s inauguration was made from repurposed PET bottles. The partnership also extends to food, with Sprite collaborating with Wow! Momo as part of the onboard experience. ‘New engaging experience for passengers’ Abhishek Gupta, Vice President, Customer Development, Coca-Cola India & Southwest Asia, said the association with IRCTC would help Sprite explore new opportunities within the travel ecosystem and create a more engaging experience for passengers. Ajit Kumar Sinha, Chief Regional Manager, Lucknow Division, IRCTC, said the partnership brings an established consumer brand into the travel environment through an integrated onboard experience.

articles.title: Gurugram's Exicom makes India's first liquid-cooled EV charger modules in Hyderabad
articles.content: Home Trending News Gurugram’s Exicom makes India’s first liquid-cooled EV charger modules in Hyderabad Gurugram’s Exicom makes India’s first liquid-cooled EV charger modules in Hyderabad Gurugram-based Exicom-Tele Systems has started manufacturing what it calls India’s first liquid-cooled AC and DC power modules for EV chargers at its Hyderabad facility. By Devanshu Srivastava 21 Aug 2026 Follow Us New Update A view of Exicom's facility Gurugram-based Exicom-Tele Systems has started manufacturing what it calls India’s first liquid-cooled AC and DC power modules for EV chargers at its Hyderabad facility. The company said the development marks a significant milestone in its power electronics business and will support EV charging requirements in global markets, including North America and Europe. Exicom Starts Manufacturing Liquid-Cooled Power Modules The new power modules are being manufactured at Exicom’s recently inaugurated Hyderabad Smart Manufacturing Facility, which uses automation, digital traceability and specialised testing systems. The technology builds on the liquid-cooled capabilities of Tritium, the global DC fast-charging company acquired by Exicom in 2024. Advertisment Add Startup Pedia As A Trusted Source The modules will initially be used in Tritium’s DC charging portfolio, including its TRI-FLEX ultra-fast DC chargers and DC-FLEX charging systems. Exicom said the initial production will primarily cater to customers in North America and Europe , while the company plans to eventually use the technology across its EV charging products for Charge Point Operators, fleets and OEMs in India. Liquid Cooling Helps Manage Heat in High-Power Charging According to Exicom, liquid cooling addresses one of the key challenges in high-power EV charging: heat. The company said nearly 60% of power electronics failures are linked to thermal stress, while a 10°C to 15°C increase in temperature can double component failure rates. Liquid-cooled systems use coolant to transfer heat more efficiently than air-cooled systems. Exicom said its technology can keep internal temperatures around 10°C lower. The sealed architecture also helps protect components from dust, moisture and salt air, which can improve their suitability for different operating environments. Also read: 'By 2028, we want to see these fly,' says Aviation Minister as India plans electric taxi launch with Sarla Aviation Exicom Plans to Expand Liquid-Cooled Technology Exicom plans to incorporate liquid-cooled architecture into its flagship Harmony DC chargers over time. The company said this could also create a new line of power electronics exports from India, with the Hyderabad facility supporting both domestic and international production. The development also strengthens the integration between Exicom and Tritium. Following the acquisition, Exicom is combining Tritium’s liquid-cooling technology with its own manufacturing capabilities to develop and produce EV charging equipment in India. articles.title: India's First Large-Scale Biopolymer Plant Set for October Launch: Transforming Sugarcane ...
articles.content: India's green manufacturing sector is on the verge of achieving a historic feat. Set to be operational by October 2026, the country’s first biopolymer facility by Balrampur Chini Mills Limited (BCML) is coming up rapidly at the Kumbhi sugar unit in the Lakhimpur Kheri district of Uttar Pradesh. The fully integrated greenfield project, involving an investment of more than ₹3,080 crores, means a major advancement in the world of sustainable materials. The new plant is operating under the Balrampur Bioyug brand, will convert locally sourced sugarcane directly into Polylactic Acid (PLA), which is a biodegradable bioplastic that breaks down in nature in months. Using only renewable energy and employing a zero liquid discharge (ZLD) system, the initiative is intended to reduce the use of single-use plastics and make Uttar Pradesh the pioneer of the revolution of bio-economy in India. Watch the CNBC-TV18 report on the plant for PLA bioplastics Key highlights of Project Geographical Advantage: The facility will be developed as a complete manufacturing plant within the premises of BCML’s sugar mill situated at Kumbhi in Gola Gokarannath. Huge Investment: The investment in the project is estimated at around ₹2,850 crore to ₹3,080 crore, making Uttar Pradesh a centre of excellence for green technology. Sophisticated Production Capabilities: The plant will have an annual production capacity of 80,000 tonnes of Polylactic acid (PLA) once it becomes operational. Inauguration: The Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh laid the foundation stone for the large project on February 22, 2025. From Sugarcane to Bioplastics: How It Works From Sugarcane to Bioplastics: The plant works based on a closed-system approach. First, sugarcane is farmed and turned into sugar. Instead of sending the entire output to food markets, most of the output goes to the manufacture of Polylactic Acid (PLA). Whereas traditional plastics take hundreds of years to disintegrate, products made using the plant, such as plates, cups, bottles, pens, and carry bags, decompose naturally in a time span ranging from three to six months. Moreover, many cutting-edge technologies from companies such as Sulzer from Switzerland and Alpine can be utilized at the plant. Impacts on Environment and Economy Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD): To protect the environment, the manufacturing campus is outfitted with Zero Liquid Discharge technology, stopping any toxic wastewater from being dumped into local drains or reservoirs. Use of Renewable Energy Sources: The entire processing plant has been developed to utilize renewable energy sources in order to assist the Indian government in achieving zero carbon emissions. Impact on the Local Economy: Connecting local agriculture with modern manufacturing helps create jobs in local regions and protect farmers by diversifying their crops. Since the beginning of the commercial production of bioplastics right after the October commissioning, India is making a move from traditional packaging towards a circular economy.

articles.title: India's first large-scale biopolymer plant in UP set for October launch, ETManufacturing
articles.content: Chemicals 1 min read India's first large-scale biopolymer plant in UP set for October launch This pioneering project will convert locally grown sugarcane into PLA-based bioplastic. The facility features a Zero Liquid Discharge system to prevent harmful liquid waste. PTI Published On Aug 21, 2026 at 01:00 PM IST Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook India's first large-scale biopolymer plant in Lakhimpur Kheri is nearing its October operational launch. India's first large-scale biopolymer plant, being built at an investment of ₹3,080 crore in Lakhimpur Kheri district, is likely to become operational in October, officials said. Kheri District Magistrate Anjani Kumar Singh on Thursday inspected the under-construction plant and reviewed its progress ahead of its proposed launch in October. Singh said the entire manufacturing process, from locally grown sugarcane to Polylactic Acid (PLA)-based bioplastic, would take place on a single campus. "The pioneering project will add a new chapter to Kheri's agriculture-based industrial development and provide a new direction to sustainable and eco-friendly industrial growth in the area," he said. Advt During the inspection plant officials gave a presentation on the facility's layout and various stages of production. The District Magistrate examined the process of converting sugarcane into sugar and subsequently into PLA bioplastic and sought details about technical aspects and production workflows. A major feature of the facility is its Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) system, which is designed to ensure that no harmful liquid waste is discharged into rivers or drains, officials said. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had laid the foundation stone for the plant at the Kumbhi sugar unit of Balrampur Chini Mills in Gola Gokarannath on February 22, 2025. During his visit, Adityanath had said the project would promote environment-friendly products and create employment opportunities for local youth. articles.title: India's telecom manufacturing zone attracts $655 million - Bisinfotech
articles.content: The efforts made towards making India a leading country in hardware manufacturing have now seen success as India has made great strides. The Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) project to be created in Gwalior city, Madhya Pradesh has already gotten more than ₹5,500 crore ($655 million) investments. It is projected that, through the huge investment, about 18,000 jobs would be created, thereby significantly helping the Indian technology and manufacturing sectors. The recent investments came about after the holding of two rounds of industrial round tables in Mumbai. The two rounds of talks were organized through the collaborative efforts of DoT and COAI. The two rounds of talks were presided over by Jyotiraditya M. Scindia (Union Communications Minister), Mohan Yadav (Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh) and Amit Agrawal (DoT Secretary). The two rounds of talks have formed a part and parcel of the government’s efforts aimed at achieving the objective of Aatmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India) initiative. This is due to the fact that through the setting up of the TMZ, the government wants to improve manufacturing capacity, export levels, reduce importation of costly hardware and create a competitive electronics environment. Strong Investor Support Across Two Major Summits Financial commitments to the Gwalior TMZ can be divided into two separate stages: Fractal Systems Launches M2G Architecture for Mesh-to-Satellite Connectivity Also Read Mumbai Investor Roundtable: International tech firms and regional telecom companies committed more than ₹2,000 crore (about $238 million). The first wave of financing from Mumbai is set to create over 4,000 jobs. Delhi Investor Roundtable: In an earlier roundtable that took place in New Delhi, investors had committed about ₹3,500 crore (about $417 million) in investment offers with 14,000 job opportunities. Together, these commitments amount to more than ₹5,500 crore and 18,000 potential job opportunities. Global Tech Giants and Local Telecom Leaders Jump Onboard Several major foreign technology companies, including Nokia, Ericsson, and Qualcomm, have shown interest in the establishment of their business establishments in Gwalior. Major Indian IT services companies such as TCS and Tech Mahindra have also conveyed that they intend to develop manufacturing factories, global service units, and research centers in the special economic zone. Qualcomm Appoints Sergio Buniac to Lead Mobile, Compute and Personal AI Division Also Read The three prominent private telecommunication companies in India, namely Bharti Airtel, Reliance Jio, and Vodafone Idea, have fully supported the project. Apart from this, these companies have conveyed their commitment to encourage their equipment manufacturers to operate in the Gwalior special economic zone. A Modern, Plug-and-Play Hub for Telecommunications The foundation stone for establishing Gwalior TMZ was officially laid down on July 30, 2026, through the signing of the MoU by the Department of Telecommunications with the Madhya Pradesh State Government. articles.title: India's First Large-Scale Sugarcane-Based Biopolymer Plant In Uttar Pradesh Nears Launch
articles.content: Aug 21, 2026 | Updated 02:04 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . India's first industrial-scale biopolymer manufacturing plant in Uttar Pradesh is scheduled for commissioning in October 2026, marking a significant milestone in the country's shift towards sustainable manufacturing. The facility, being built by Balrampur Chini Mills Limited in Kumbhi, Lakhimpur Kheri district, represents a gross investment of Rs 2,850 crore and will produce polylactic acid biopolymers from sugarcane. The state-of-the-art facility will have an annual production capacity of 80,000 tonnes and will run entirely on renewable energy. Located adjacent to BCML's existing sugar factory, the plant will transform sugarcane directly into fully compostable, bio-based plastic alternatives. This integrated approach enhances resource efficiency by sourcing raw materials from the adjacent sugar mill, optimising supply chain management. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath laid the foundation stone for the facility in February 2025, positioning the state as the epicentre of India's biopolymer revolution. The project aims to support India's net zero emissions target by providing eco-friendly alternatives to single-use plastics in packaging, biomedical applications, food service ware, textiles and various industrial applications. The facility leverages cutting-edge technology from global providers including Alpine from Austria and Sulzer from Switzerland. BCML's PLA vertical, branded as Balrampur Bioyug, has already secured its first institutional order from the Lucknow Cantonment Board for compostable products including garbage bags, bottles and pens, reflecting institutional confidence ahead of the plant's commissioning. Manufacturing one kilogram of PLA currently requires around 1.6 kilograms of sugar, though technological improvements could reduce this to 1.2 kilograms in the future. The project is financed through 40 per cent equity and 60 per cent debt, and the company aims for PLA and other non-sugar businesses to contribute about 50 per cent of its revenue within three years of the plant's full operation. articles.title: Treesa Jolly, Gayatri Gopichand confirm India's first medal at BWF World Championships
articles.content: Treesa Jolly, Gayatri Gopichand confirm India’s first medal at BWF World Championships Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand defeated China’s Y.F. Jia and S.X. Zhang in the women’s doubles quarterfinal. Updated on: Aug 21, 2026, 14:00:14 IST By Aditya Maheshwari Prefer HT on Google Share via Copy link Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand continued their underdog story and confirmed India’s first medal at the BWF World Championships 2026. It was a performance Treesa and Gayatri can be extremely proud of, as they overcame fourth-seeded Zhang Shuxian and Jia Yifan in their quarter-final. The Indian pair lost the first game but produced a stellar comeback, winning the next two to seal a 16-21, 21-15, 21-13 victory. India's Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand are in the semifinal (Reuters) Treesa and Gayatri displayed true character in a battle where few had given them a chance before the clash. Zhang and Jia showed throughout why they are among the world’s top five, but the Indian shuttlers refused to let them dictate the contest for long. Also Read: Lessons from India Open, 3,000 workers and a bigger test - How BAI got its act right for World Badminton Championships The momentum kept shifting like a pendulum, as both pairs fought for control and the crowd stayed firmly behind the Indians. Even when the Chinese pair had the upper hand, Treesa and Gayatri kept finding a way back into the match. What followed was a performance full of belief, composure and fighting spirit. The Indian pair held their nerve when it mattered most, completing a memorable comeback and securing a World Championships medal in front of a roaring home crowd. It was also pleasing to see a big turnout at the Indira Gandhi Arena for an afternoon match, with two young shuttlers fighting hard to keep India’s medal hopes alive in the women’s category. From survival to success Treesa, Gayatri struggled at the start of the first game, allowing the Chinese pair to establish a solid lead. However, with their backs against the wall, Gayatri and Treesa composed themselves and launched a comeback. They fought their way back to 14-16, bringing the packed arena into the contest. The game went down to the wire, with the crowd throwing its full support behind the Indian pair. But in a topsy-turvy battle, the Chinese pair regained control at the crucial stage to take the opening game 21-16. What had started as another uphill battle turned into a fiercely contested game, with the Indian pair showing tremendous composure under pressure.
